name: Juvederm Volbella
lead: Juvéderm Volbella (VYC-15L; Volbella XC with lidocaine) is a low-concentration cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) filler from Allergan, made with Vycross technology and used for fine lines and delicate areas, chiefly the lips and perioral region and the under-eye hollow (infraorbital) area. [1][2] People choose it to add soft volume and smooth fine lines around the mouth, which changes lip shape, the look of vertical lip lines and the contour of the hollow beneath the eye.

Randomized and open-label trials report improvement in lip fullness out to 12 months, and trials in infraorbital hollowing have been run in the US and China. [3][4][5] Reports of delayed reactions in the tear-trough area and lips have also been published. [6]

paras: The product is a 15 mg/mL HA gel formulated with Vycross technology; a postmarket lip study used the lidocaine version. [2] Laboratory comparisons of seven cross-linking technologies tested properties such as cohesivity and resistance to compression across HA gels. [7] A review discusses Voluma, Volift and Volbella together as a Vycross range suited to different depths and areas. [8]

Hyaluronic acid is a sugar molecule found naturally in skin and joints; Wikipedia traces the discovery of its role in skin hydration to Karl Meyer and John Palmer at Columbia University in 1934, and its first use for facial tissue augmentation to Europe in 1996.[17] Most hyaluronic acid fillers are chemically cross-linked, commonly with BDDE, so the gel lasts longer than uncross-linked hyaluronic acid.[18] The US FDA approved the first Juvéderm product in June 2006, on the basis of a comparison with a collagen filler in which 88 percent of subjects preferred the Juvéderm side.[17]
Lip and perioral enhancement and infraorbital hollowing are the main studied uses. [3][4][5][9]

Lip augmentation is among the main appearance uses of Juvéderm-brand fillers, because lips lose volume and definition with age; Wikipedia also lists smoothing wrinkles and filling hollows and scars.[17] Wikipedia reports effects from filler of this kind typically lasting about six to nine months for Juvéderm products, with repeat injections needed to maintain the result, while the registered and published Volbella studies followed lips for up to 12 months.[17][4] Treatments are performed by a clinician rather than at home.

Trials of Volbella measure results on Allergan's Lip Fullness Scale, where a responder is someone who improves by at least one point, and on patient-reported FACE-Q scales for satisfaction with lips and lip lines.[10][12]

In a randomized study of 225 adults with minimal, mild or moderate lip fullness, VYC-15L met its non-inferiority endpoint against Restylane-L: at month 3 the responder rate was 80.3% for VYC-15L versus 70.8% for the comparator, and it stayed above 60% through one year. Perioral line severity improved in 65.4% of VYC-15L subjects at month 3 and 66.2% at one year, and 96.1% and 88.2% reported improved satisfaction with lips and lip lines at month 3. Severe injection-site responses were reported less often with VYC-15L than the comparator.[4]

An earlier randomized trial of 280 subjects (Volbella with lidocaine versus Restylane-L) was also non-inferior at three months, with investigator assessments showing greater improvement in lip fullness, perioral lines and oral commissures at months 6 to 12, and less acute swelling.[10] In the repeat-treatment study of 124 subjects, responder rates were 86.2%, 80.3% and 65.3% at months 1, 3 and 12 after initial treatment; after repeat treatment at one year the rate rose to 94.3% at one month, with a lower median volume (1.5 versus 2.6 mL), and FACE-Q scores doubled from baseline.[12] The 60-subject European open-label study followed participants at 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months, with a prespecified month 3 responder target.[3]

A retrospective study of 400 patients reported that a newly introduced filler in the tear-trough area and lips was associated with a higher rate of late reactions, with persistent and recurrent courses, than the 0.02% rate recorded for HA fillers generally. [6]

Wikipedia lists temporary redness, pain, swelling and bruising as common effects of Juvéderm injection, and immune reactions producing lumps (granulomas) as a less common effect; Allergan advises against use in people with severe allergies or a history of anaphylaxis.[17] The dermal filler article describes vascular complications as a serious but uncommon risk: filler entering a blood vessel can block the ophthalmic or retinal arteries, which can cause permanent blindness, and delayed skin necrosis can also occur, with embolic events reported more often with autologous fat than with hyaluronic acid.[18]

In the United States the FDA regulates dermal fillers as medical devices and the injection is performed by a licensed provider; Wikipedia says only a small number of fillers are approved there.[18] In the UK and European Economic Area fillers are non-prescription medical devices requiring a CE mark, which addresses manufacturing standards rather than proven efficacy, and more than 140 fillers are on sale.[18] China's NMPA has issued guidance on regulating fillers, and the Volbella trials in Chinese adults listed under Clinical studies relate to that market.[18][15][16]

A 12-month multicenter open-label study of 60 subjects treated the perioral area and used a lip fullness responder endpoint. [3] A postmarket study of 62 subjects evaluated aesthetic impact in the lips. [2] Randomized, controlled studies followed lip and perioral enhancement for 12 months. [4][10][11] A repeat-treatment study examined retreatment safety. [12] An open-label study evaluated infraorbital skin depressions. [5]
Registered trials include lip comparisons with Restylane-L (n=285), a lip study with 225 participants and Chinese lip (n=176) and infraorbital (n=160) studies. [13][14][15][16]

timeline.event: Karl Meyer and John Palmer identify hyaluronic acid's role in skin hydration.[17]
Hyaluronic acid first used for facial augmentation in Europe.[17]
FDA approves the first Juvéderm product.[17]
12-month European open-label study of Volbella in the perioral area published.[3]
Randomized trial of Volbella with lidocaine versus Restylane-L published.[10]
One-year randomized results for VYC-15L (Volbella XC) and infraorbital open-label study published.[4][5]

card.summary: Allergan's fine HA filler for lips and under-eye hollows, backed by randomized trials, with reports of late reactions in the tear-trough area.
card.note: Delayed reactions reported in tear-trough and lip treatment.

quick.overview:
Volbella is a thin, low-concentration hyaluronic acid filler used for lip enhancement, perioral lines and under-eye hollows.

Trials of up to 12 months report improved lip fullness, and infraorbital studies have been run in the US and China.
quick.mechanism: A lightly cross-linked HA gel (Vycross) is placed superficially to add soft volume and smooth fine lines; it degrades over time.
quick.risks: Reported effects include swelling and bruising; one retrospective report described recurrent delayed reactions in the tear-trough area and lips. It is a prescription device given by licensed clinicians.
